claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for launch because aggregate release readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public governance guidance permits certification with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring despite the unresolved small-business onboarding gap.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence shows the materiality predicate is not met, or the limitation was disclosed, or approved risk acceptance was granted before launch.
Evidence of aggregate readiness may support operational readiness, but it cannot override a policy-triggered disclosure requirement for a named contractual or launch segment.
Generic public guidance can support documentation and monitoring practices, but it cannot substitute for satisfaction of the internal policy threshold in this case.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the small-business onboarding gap requires disclosure.
Provide the final model card or launch disclosure showing the named limitation was disclosed for the affected launch use case.
Provide an approved risk-acceptance record covering this material limitation before launch, if one exists.
Provide any formal policy exception or approval authorizing certification despite the unresolved named-segment gap.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a named-segment evaluation gap: the small-business onboarding segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two paid pilot commitments.
The governing policy states a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; that predicate appears satisfied on the current record.
There is no admissible evidence that the material limitation was disclosed before launch, resolved before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Legal review is still open on whether disclosure is required, which leaves a required policy predicate unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not resolve materiality for a named launch use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently policy-compliant on the available record.
That public model-card and risk-management guidance is sufficient to satisfy the specific internal disclosure policy for this case.
That launch-ready certification can be defended without evidence of disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a final legal/policy determination.
